blockingIssues.description: The new raw_manifest path never creates the target namespace before running `kubectl apply`. VAL-ENGINE-008's canonical case is a ConfigMap manifest in namespace `cts-raw`; with this implementation, a scenario that sets `namespace: cts-raw` will fail with a missing-namespace error instead of exiting 0. The helm path handles this by creating the namespace first, but the raw_manifest path does not.

nonBlockingIssues.description: The new bats coverage for `apply-scenario.sh` is mostly grep-based and never executes the script or `kubectl`. The dispatch, unknown-kind, tempfile-cleanup, and URL-handling checks only assert that certain strings exist in the source, so they do not actually verify VAL-ENGINE-008 or the cleanup side effects.

codeReview.summary: The schema split and backward-compatibility work look reasonable, but the runtime `raw_manifest` implementation misses namespaced resources, so the feature does not satisfy the namespaced ConfigMap case in VAL-ENGINE-008. The added tests are too shallow to catch that runtime failure because they mostly inspect source text instead of executing the new path.

issues.description: In `apply_raw_manifest`, lines 97-102 only append `--namespace` to the `kubectl apply` command. There is no `kubectl get ns ... || kubectl create ns ...` equivalent here, even though the helm branch does that at line 135. As a result, raw manifests targeting a fresh namespace (including the validation contract's `cts-raw` ConfigMap example) fail before the feature's core behavior can succeed.

The runtime tests added for `apply-scenario.sh` do not run the script. Lines 241-280 only grep for function names and error strings, so they do not exercise declared-order application, unknown-kind rejection at runtime, tempfile cleanup behavior, or actual `kubectl apply` success. That gap is why the missing-namespace bug above went undetected.
